question: According to an official report released in April 2025, AI-based real-time forest monitoring system has been implemented for the first time in which state sensitive forest divisions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, Madhya Pradesh became the first state to implement an **AI-based real-time forest monitoring system** in its sensitive forest divisions.
 
• This system leverages cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology to monitor forest cover and prevent illegal activities such as deforestation and poaching.
 
• The initiative enhances the state's ability to track changes in forest density, detect forest fires, and respond to environmental threats in real-time.
 
• The project focuses on sensitive forest divisions, including **protected areas and wildlife sanctuaries**, ensuring the preservation of biodiversity.
 
• This innovative step aligns with India's commitments to combat climate change and achieve sustainable development goals through enhanced forest conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam**

 
 
• Assam is known for its rich biodiversity and unique forest ecosystems, including Kaziranga National Park and Manas Wildlife Sanctuary.
 
• While it has implemented forest conservation measures, it has not been the first state to adopt AI-based real-time forest monitoring.
 
• Assam is also addressing challenges like human-wildlife conflict and illegal logging through traditional and digital monitoring methods.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**
 
 
• Odisha is home to extensive forest areas and wildlife reserves, including Similipal National Park and Bhitarkanika National Park.
 
• The state employs technologies such as GIS and remote sensing for forest management but has not pioneered AI-based real-time monitoring systems.
 
• Odisha is also recognized for its efforts in mangrove restoration and climate resilience projects.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**
 
 
• Gujarat has significant forest cover, including the Gir National Park, which is the last refuge of the Asiatic lion.
 
• The state utilizes advanced surveillance systems for wildlife protection but has not yet implemented AI-based real-time forest monitoring across its divisions.
 
• Efforts in Gujarat are focused on wildlife conservation and habitat restoration.
